land.text: the Habsburg domains turned by the Compromise of 1867 'into a real union'; Cliopatria's first Austria-Hungary shape, 1868

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Austrian Empire row runs to 1867 and its Austria-Hungary row starts in 1868. The infobox also lists the Bosnia vilayet as preceded-by, which is the 1878 occupation recorded in the ledger.

land.text: Czechia and Slovakia: 'Czech politicians peacefully took over command in Prague on 28 October'; 'On the same day, the Czechs and Slovaks formally proclaimed the establishment of Czechoslovakia as an independent state'; 'On 30 October, the Slovaks did the same'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Czechoslovakia row starts 1919; the page lists Czechoslovakia as a successor and gives no frontier. The czechoslovakia dossier founds the state in October 1918 on Bohemia, Moravia and Slovakia (/ledger/0); Carpathian Ruthenia reaches it from hungarian-republic in April 1919 (/ledger/2) and Cieszyn Silesia is divided with Poland (/ledger/1, /ledger/4).

land.text: Austria: the German-Austrian National Council 'proclaimed the Republic of German Austria'; the State Council was created on 30 October 1918 as the executive body

successors.note: Cliopatria's Republic of Austria row starts 1919. The infobox successor is German-Austria (proclaimed a republic 12 November 1918; renamed Republic of Austria on 21 October 1919 after the Treaty of Saint-Germain of 10 September 1919, German-Austria page). German-Austria's own claim of 22 November 1918 ('all the majority-German territory of the former Habsburg realm', 118,311 km2) was larger than present Austria and is not drawn; Burgenland ('most of Burgenland, which became part of Austria', Trianon page) lies inside the 1912 outline.

land.text: Hungary and Carpathian Ruthenia: Karolyi 'formally repudiate[d] the compromise agreement on 31 October' and proclaimed the Hungarian Democratic Republic on 16 November; Carpathian Ruthenia stayed Hungarian until April 1919 (czechoslovakia dossier /ledger/2)

successors.note: Cliopatria's Hungarian Republic row starts 1919 and is larger than the present country; the page gives no frontier before the Treaty of Trianon (4 June 1920). Carpathian Ruthenia ('which became part of Czechoslovakia', Trianon page) is listed here because the czechoslovakia dossier gains it from hungarian-republic in April 1919. Lands that went to Romania, Czechoslovakia, the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and Austria are in those successors' entries.

land.text: the South Slav lands: 'On 29 October, the Slavs in both portions of what remained of Austria-Hungary proclaimed the' State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs; Istria goes to Italy (next entry); the three cells of the outline that lie in modern Montenegro are the Dalmatian coast (reading)

successors.note: No Cliopatria row; the state needs a dossier (it joined the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, the page's other successor, slug yugoslavia). Saint-Germain page: 'Most of Dalmatia, Carniola, and Lower Styria' ceded to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and 'Also Bosnia and Herzegovina was given to it'; Trianon page: 'Croatia-Slavonia was included in a newly formed State of Slovenes, Croats, and Serbs' and Vendvidek (now Prekmurje) became part of the Kingdom. The Slovenian part of the Austrian Littoral cannot be named with the gazetteer and stays in this entry although Saint-Germain gives the Littoral to Italy.

land.text: Trentino, South Tyrol and the Austrian Littoral: 'The southern half of the former Tyrolean crownland up to the Brenner Pass' and 'the Austrian Littoral' with Trieste and Istria went to Italy (Saint-Germain, 10 September 1919)

successors.note: Infobox successor. The Villa Giusti armistice was signed on 3 November 1918; the lands were annexed in 1919 (kingdom-of-italy /ledger/15: Trentino-Alto Adige and Trieste). Istria is added from the Saint-Germain page and is taken out of the Slovenes-Croats-Serbs entry.

land.text: western Galicia and the Polish part of Cieszyn Silesia: the Polish Liquidation Committee, 'Created on 28 October 1918' at Krakow, to keep order in 'the former Austrian part of partitioned Poland'; Saint-Germain: 'The former Galicia fell back to the re-established Polish Republic'

successors.note: Infobox successors 'Polish Liquidation Committee' and 'Kingdom of Poland' are folded into the Second Polish Republic (Cliopatria row from 1919; no dossier yet). The Committee 'handed over its authority to the central Polish government seated in Warsaw' on 27 March 1919. The region is the outline's cells in modern Poland: western Galicia plus the Polish part of Cieszyn Silesia, which the czechoslovakia dossier shows divided in 1920.

land.text: eastern Galicia: 'The West Ukrainian People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 November 1918' and 'controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919'; the outline's Ukrainian cells minus Carpathian Ruthenia (hungarian-republic) and Bukovina (Romania)

successors.note: Infobox successor, a state Cliopatria lacks (no dossier yet; slug proposed). The page says it 'also claimed the northern part of Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia'; neither is given to it here because Bukovina's union with Romania was declared on 28 November 1918 (Kingdom of Romania page) and Carpathian Ruthenia went to Czechoslovakia via Hungary. Act of Union with the Ukrainian People's Republic 22 January 1919; Polish forces had taken most of the claimed territory by July 1919.

land.text: Transylvania, the Romanian Banat, Crisana, Maramures and all of Bukovina: '28 November. The union of Bukovina with Romania is declared'; 'the union of Transylvania with the Kingdom of Romania on 1 December 1918'; Trianon: 'Romania received the territories of Transylvania, part of Banat and other territories from Hungary'

successors.note: Stands for Romania, as in the 1916-1918 ledger: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Romania row starts 1919 and the Romanian dossier (ending December 1918) passes to kingdom-of-romania. That dossier's /ledger/27-28 book Bukovina and Transylvania as gains from austria-hungary. Banat: Trianon page 'The central parts of Banat were later assigned to Romania'; Crisana and Maramures are named on none of the pages opened and are taken from the present Romanian frontier (reading).

land.text: Vojvodina (Banat, Backa, Baranja, Syrmia) and the Serbian bank of the Sava: the Great National Assembly at Novi Sad 'on 25 November 1918' proclaimed the secession of 'Banat, Bačka and Baranja' from the 'already collapsed Austria-Hungary' and their unification with the Kingdom of Serbia

successors.note: Stands for the Kingdom of Serbia (Cliopatria's Serbs row ends 1915; the serbs dossier runs to December 1918 and passes to yugoslavia). The serbs dossier books Syrmia on 24 November 1918 (/ledger/28) and Banat, Backa and Baranja on 25 November (/ledger/29) as gains from austria-hungary. Trianon page: 'Banat, Backa and Baranja ... came under military control by the Kingdom of Serbia'.

capitals.name: Vienna
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Vienna'. Budapest is listed only as the capital of the Kingdom of Hungary in the page's administrative table and was the seat of the Hungarian half's government; no sentence calls it a capital of the monarchy.

rulers.note: Infobox '1916-1918: Charles I and IV'; 'On 11 November, Karl issued a carefully worded proclamation'.

keyframe_review.note: 623,272 km2 for 1868-1870 against the infobox's only figure, 621,538 km2 for 1905 (ratio 1.00 for this shape; 1.09 for the 1905 shape): the Habsburg lands of both halves without Bosnia (Hungary 366 cells, Romania 409, Austria 331, Czechia 321, Ukraine 256, Slovakia 195, Croatia 190, Poland 153). The page does not say whether its figure includes Bosnia. The Austrian Empire row drops 220 Czech cells in 1866-1867 (corrected in that dossier); this shape has them.
623,140 km2, 132 km2 below 1868: two German cells gained, one Czech, one Polish and one German lost, within the grid's noise; the page records no boundary change in 1871.
623,093 km2, unchanged in extent from 1871 (same bbox); no page event.

correction.text: The 1873 outline, without Bosnia and Herzegovina or the Sanjak of Novi Pazar: 'Austria occupied (but did not annex) the provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina' in 1878; the annexation came in October 1908. Both are occupations (ledger), hatched, until then

keyframe_review.note: 677,562 km2: +54,469 km2 over 1873, 180 cells in Bosnia and Herzegovina and 16 in Serbia and Montenegro (the Sanjak). The Condominium page: 'The occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina started on 29 July 1878 and was over on 20 October'; the Austria-Hungary page: the Sanjak 'was under Austro-Hungarian occupation between 1878 and 1909'. Cliopatria draws both as Austrian land from 1880, two years after the occupation began and 28 years before the annexation.

correction.text: The 1873 outline with Bosnia and the Sanjak held as occupation until 1908 (Bosnia) and 1909 (the Sanjak)

keyframe_review.note: 677,584 km2, 22 km2 above 1880 (same bbox, noise): as for 1880, an occupation drawn as land. The infobox's 1905 figure of 621,538 km2 matches the 1873 outline (ratio 1.00), not this shape (1.09). The Tianjin concession began on 27 December 1902 (ledger gain, 1902/12, Tianjin concession page), so it is added from 1902 although Cliopatria draws it only from 1905.

correction.text: For 1905-1907: the 1873 outline plus the concession at Tianjin that Cliopatria draws from 1905 (bbox now reaches 117.5 E, 39.7 N), with Bosnia and the Sanjak still occupation; from October 1908 the annexed Bosnia is added by the 1908 keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 677,899 km2 for 1905-1910, +314 km2 over 1900 (two Chinese cells at Tianjin). The Condominium page: 'On 5 October the Emperor Franz Joseph announced the annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina' (announced in Sarajevo on 7 October 1908); the Ottoman Empire recognised it on 26 February 1909. The Sanjak was returned in 1909, a year before this shape ends. The Tianjin concession page gives 27 December 1902 as its start (ledger gain 1902/12) and 14 August 1917 as its end; Cliopatria draws the two cells from 1905.

correction.text: The 1911 outline: the 1873 lands plus the annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina (announced 5 October 1908) and the Tianjin concession, without the Sanjak of Novi Pazar, which was returned to the Ottoman Empire in 1909

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1905-1910 shape keeps the Sanjak until 1910 although the Austria-Hungary page says the Sanjak 'was returned to the Ottoman Empire' in 1909 and the Condominium page speaks of 'the Austrian-Hungarian garrisons leaving the Sanjak of Novi Pazar'. Bosnia and Herzegovina is territory from October 1908.

673,603 km2: -4,295 km2 against 1910, the 15 Sanjak cells (Serbia 9, Montenegro 6) drop out, two years after the page's 1909 return. Bosnia and Herzegovina stay, annexed 'in October 1908'. This is the outline of the 1908 keyframe.
673,580 km2 for 1912-1914, -24 km2 against 1911 (noise): the monarchy on the eve of war, the outline used below for the war-years corrections. The page's war declaration on Serbia: 28 July 1914.

correction.text: The 1912 outline: Galicia is Austro-Hungarian land held in part by Russia (occupation, in the ledger), not lost territory

keyframe_review.note: 592,349 km2, 81,231 km2 under 1914: it drops Galicia (198 Ukrainian and 121 Polish cells) and a few Romanian and Slovak cells for all of 1915. The Eastern Front page: 'the Russians controlling almost all of that region by the end of 1914' and 'In May 1915 ... the Central Powers began the successful Gorlice-Tarnow Offensive in Galicia'; the page does not date the recapture of Przemysl or Lemberg. Russian-held Austro-Hungarian land is an occupation (rule 4), not a loss.

correction.text: The 1912 outline: Serbia, Montenegro and northern Albania are occupied foreign land (hatched), Galicia's recovery and the Romanian incursion are in the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 707,975 km2: +115,626 km2 over 1915: 171 Serbian, 38 Kosovo, 47 Montenegrin and 76 Albanian cells plus Galicia's Polish cells back, minus 95 Romanian cells lost. The Serbian campaign page: the October 1915 invasion 'launched, under German command ... on 6 October 1915'; 'Serbia was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria'; the Montenegrin campaign page: Lovcen attacked on 8 January 1916, Cetinje reached on 13 January, 'Scutari and finally Durazzo at the end of February'. These are occupations of other states' land, not Austro-Hungarian territory.

correction.text: The 1912 outline without the Tianjin concession; Romanian Wallachia is occupied (ledger), not annexed

keyframe_review.note: 854,648 km2: +146,673 km2 over 1916: 455 Romanian cells (Transylvania back plus Wallachia and the Dobruja zone), 127 Ukrainian cells (Galicia and Bukovina recovered), 7 Bulgarian; it loses 25 Albanian cells and the two Chinese cells. The Austria-Hungary page: 'On 27 August 1916, Romania declared war against Austria-Hungary. ... On 6 December, Bucharest was captured'; the Eastern Front page: 'on 27 August, Romanian troops marched into Transylvania' and the Kerensky offensive of 29 June 1917 was thrown back as the Austrians 'drove them almost entirely out of Austria-Hungary'. Cliopatria draws Wallachia as Austrian land; it was a joint Central Powers occupation. The Chinese cells' loss is the revocation of the Tianjin concession on 14 August 1917 (ledger). The remainder of Galicia and Bukovina was Russian-held until August 1917 (Kerensky Offensive page: Tarnopol 25 July, Czernowitz 3 August).

correction.text: The 1912 outline without the Tianjin concession; the occupied Romanian, Ukrainian and Italian zones are in the ledger, not territory

keyframe_review.note: 931,840 km2: +77,192 km2 over 1917: 113 Moldovan, 76 Romanian, 59 Ukrainian and 54 Italian cells. The Eastern Front page: 'on 3 March 1918, the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was signed' 'after Operation Faustschlag', the Central Powers 'concluded a military treaty with Ukraine', and 'On 7 May 1918 Romania signed the Treaty of Bucharest'; the Austria-Hungary page: Caporetto on 24 October 1917 and the Villa Giusti armistice on 3 November 1918. The page does not map the Austro-Hungarian zones in Ukraine, Moldova or Romania, nor the Italian front line, so those cells are unverified: page budget. Second pass: Operation Faustschlag page dates the offensive 18 February - 3 March 1918 and says Ukrainian troops and the Austro-Hungarian Army 'had secured Odessa', but maps no zone; at 31 October 1918 the 1912 outline passes to nine successors (ledger splits, identity.successors).

region.text: the Habsburg domains, the Austrian and Hungarian halves

ledger.note: 30 March 1867: the Compromise creates Austria-Hungary. Infobox '1867 Compromise: 30 March 1867'; 'The Compromise of 1867 turned the Habsburg domains into a real union between the Austrian Empire' and the Kingdom of Hungary. The page gives no boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 1868 shape.

region.text: the Sanjak of Novi Pazar: the Serbian and Montenegrin cells that Cliopatria adds in 1880 beyond the 1873 outline

ledger.note: 1878: Austria-Hungary occupies the Sanjak of Novi Pazar. The Sanjak 'was under Austro-Hungarian occupation between 1878 and 1909, when it was returned to the Ottoman Empire.' The page gives no month.

region.text: the provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina

ledger.note: 29 July 1878: Austria-Hungary occupies Bosnia and Herzegovina. 'The occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina started on 29 July 1878 and was over on 20 October.' The Austria-Hungary page: at the Congress of Berlin 'Austria occupied (but did not annex) the provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina'.

region.text: the Austro-Hungarian concession at Tianjin, 108 hectares (about 1.08 km2)

ledger.note: 27 December 1902: the concession 'formally began' (the infobox says 'Established: 1901'; the article elsewhere says it was obtained 'after the signing of the Boxer Protocol'). Area 108 hectares. Cliopatria draws two cells at Tianjin only from 1905; the 5 km circle is the gazetteer's smallest named radius. Confidence 2 because the page gives two years.

region.text: the provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina

ledger.note: 5-7 October 1908: the occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina becomes annexation. 'On 5 October the Emperor Franz Joseph announced the annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina'; announced in Sarajevo 'two days later, on 7 October'.

region.text: the provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina

ledger.note: 5 October 1908: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina, 'establishing the Condominium of Bosnia and Herzegovina'; the Ottoman Empire recognised the annexation 'on 26 February 1909' (Austria-Hungary page: 'Bosnian Crisis: 6 October 1908').

region.text: the Sanjak of Novi Pazar: the Serbian and Montenegrin cells that Cliopatria adds in 1880 beyond the 1873 outline

ledger.note: 1909: the Sanjak of Novi Pazar returns to the Ottoman Empire. 'was under Austro-Hungarian occupation between 1878 and 1909, when it was returned to the Ottoman Empire'; the Condominium page adds the garrisons leaving it after the Ottoman recognition of 26 February 1909. Cliopatria keeps it to 1910.

region.text: the part of Galicia that Cliopatria's 1916 shape holds again (western Galicia and part of the east)

ledger.note: 1914: Russia invades Galicia. 'the Russians controlling almost all of that region by the end of 1914'; the page says Russian troops also 'occupied Chernivtsi' (Bukovina) without a date. Recorded in this dossier with the occupier as counterpart (the owner's side). This start is for the part of Galicia retaken in May 1915.

region.text: the remainder of Galicia (101 cells) still missing from Cliopatria's 1916 shape, held by Russia until 1917

ledger.note: 1914: the same Russian invasion, for the remainder of Galicia and Bukovina that Cliopatria's 1916 shape still lacks and that Russia held until 1917 (the Brusilov Offensive of June 1916 forced the Austro-Hungarian 2nd and 3rd Armies back again).

region.text: the part of Galicia that Cliopatria's 1916 shape holds again (western Galicia and part of the east)

ledger.note: May 1915: the Central Powers' offensive retakes Galicia. 'In May 1915, to eliminate the Russian threat the Central Powers began the successful Gorlice-Tarnow Offensive in Galicia.' The page dates neither Przemysl (which 'fell in March 1915' on the Austria-Hungary page) nor Lemberg's recapture.

region.text: the Austro-Hungarian Military General Government of Lublin, which 'covered the southern parts of Russian Poland'

ledger.note: 1 September 1915: the Austro-Hungarian Military General Government of Lublin (infobox 'Established: 1 September 1915'; the army formed it on 25 August 1915 as the 'General Government of Kielce'; seat Kielce, then Lublin). It 'covered the southern parts of Russian Poland'; the page names no provinces, so the Lublin and Swietokrzyskie voivodeships are the researcher's reading. Cliopatria draws no Austro-Hungarian shape there. The congress-poland dossier (/ledger/8) records the same 1915/9 loss to a 'Military Government of Lublin' without naming the occupier.

region.text: Serbia, which 'was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria': the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape in Serbia, Kosovo and North Macedonia beyond the 1912 outline (Vojvodina was already Hungarian)

ledger.note: 6 October 1915: the Central Powers invade Serbia. The offensive was 'launched, under German command, almost a year later, on 6 October 1915' (Austria-Hungary declared war on 28 July 1914).

region.text: Serbia, which 'was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria': the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape in Serbia, Kosovo and North Macedonia beyond the 1912 outline (Vojvodina was already Hungarian)

ledger.note: 24 November 1915: the Serbian campaign ends. 'Mackensen declared an end to the campaign on 24 November 1915'; the result was the Great Retreat through Montenegro and Albania.

region.text: Serbia, which 'was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria': the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape in Serbia, Kosovo and North Macedonia beyond the 1912 outline (Vojvodina was already Hungarian)

ledger.note: Autumn 1915: Serbia is occupied. 'Serbia was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria'; the page gives no date for the division, so the month is the campaign's end.

region.text: Montenegro, which Austria-Hungary 'defeated and occupied' in January 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape beyond the 1912 outline

ledger.note: 8 January 1916: Austria-Hungary attacks Mount Lovcen. 'On 8 January 1916 a new attack against Montenegrin forces on Mt. Lovcen began with a massive artillery bombardment'; Lovcen was Austrian by 11 January.

region.text: Montenegro, which Austria-Hungary 'defeated and occupied' in January 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape beyond the 1912 outline

ledger.note: 17 January 1916: Montenegro falls. 'On 13 January 1916, the vanguard of the Austrian army reached the Montenegrin capital Cetinje'; armistice talks began on 13 January; infobox '5-17 January 1916', 'Austro-Hungarian victory'.

region.text: Montenegro, which Austria-Hungary 'defeated and occupied' in January 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape beyond the 1912 outline

ledger.note: January 1916: Montenegro is occupied. Austria-Hungary 'defeated and occupied the Kingdom of Montenegro'; 'On 1 March a provisional military government was established under Viktor Weber Edler von Webenau'.

region.text: northern Albania, where the troops took 'Scutari and finally Durazzo at the end of February' 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape

ledger.note: End of February 1916: Austro-Hungarian troops take Scutari and Durazzo. The troops took 'Scutari and finally Durazzo at the end of February'; the page gives no occupation zone for Albania, so the region is Cliopatria's 1916 Albanian cells.

region.text: Transylvania and southern Bukovina: the 102 Romanian cells that Cliopatria's 1916 shape loses against 1912 (Romanian troops marched into Transylvania on 27 August 1916)

ledger.note: 27 August 1916: Romania invades Transylvania. 'on 27 August, Romanian troops marched into Transylvania'; 'On 3 September, the first troops of the Central Powers marched into Romanian territory'. The Romanian state's Cliopatria row (united-principalities-of-moldavia-and-wallachia) ends in 1916.

region.text: Transylvania and southern Bukovina: the 102 Romanian cells that Cliopatria's 1916 shape loses against 1912 (Romanian troops marched into Transylvania on 27 August 1916)

ledger.note: 25 October 1916: 'by 25 October the Romanian army was back to its initial positions' (Romanian Campaign page). Falkenhayn's counter-attack began on 18 September and 'on 29 September, the outnumbered Romanians began retreating'. The page names no land for the clearing, so the Transylvania and southern Bukovina region is the Cliopatria reading; the united-principalities-of-moldavia-and-wallachia dossier (/ledger/16) gives the same date.

region.text: the Romanian cells of Cliopatria's 1917 shape beyond the 1912 outline: Wallachia and the Dobruja zone after the fall of Bucharest on 6 December 1916

ledger.note: 6 December 1916: Bucharest is captured. 'On 6 December, Bucharest was captured' (Austria-Hungary page); the Eastern Front page: 'By 5 December, Bulgarian troops had crossed the Danube and were approaching the capital'. The occupation was a joint Central Powers one; the region is Cliopatria's 1917 Romanian cells, not an Austro-Hungarian zone read from a page.

region.text: the remainder of Galicia (101 cells) still missing from Cliopatria's 1916 shape, held by Russia until 1917

ledger.note: March 1917 (dossier boundary): the Russian Empire falls (russian-empire dossier /ledger/137, dissolve to russian-republic) and its hold on the remainder of Galicia and Bukovina passes to the Provisional Government, recorded in the next two events. The Eastern Front page names no date for the empire's end.

region.text: the remainder of Galicia (101 cells) still missing from Cliopatria's 1916 shape, held by Russia until 1917

ledger.note: March 1917 (bridge): the Russian-held remainder of Galicia and Bukovina continues under the Provisional Government, the state that launched the offensive of 29 June 1917 ('Russian Provisional Government'; Kerensky Offensive page). The russian-republic dossier itself starts only on 14 September 1917 (proclamation) but the russian-empire dossier hands the Empire's land to it in March; the page is silent on the continuity, hence confidence 1.

region.text: the Austro-Hungarian concession at Tianjin, 'declaring them revoked on 14 August 1917'

ledger.note: 14 August 1917: China, having declared war on Austria-Hungary and Germany, occupied the concession and declared the concessions 'revoked on 14 August 1917'; it was handed over at 16:00 that day. Austria renounced its rights on 10 September 1919 (Saint-Germain) and Hungary on 4 June 1920 (Trianon); the page's introduction says the concession was occupied until 1920, its body and infobox say 1917. Cliopatria's 1917 shape also drops the two Chinese cells.

region.text: the remainder of Galicia (101 cells) still missing from Cliopatria's 1916 shape, held by Russia until 1917

ledger.note: 3 August 1917: 'The Germans launched their counteroffensive against the Southwestern Front on 19 July', 'Austro-German troops took the city of Tarnopol on 25 July' and Czernowitz 'fell on 3 August'; 'Most of the Austro-Hungarian provinces of Galicia and Bukovina were retaken'; Kornilov stabilised the front 'by mid-August'. The month is the fall of Czernowitz; the page gives no single date for the end of the occupation.

region.text: Friuli and the Veneto plain beyond the 1912 outline, taken after Caporetto (24 October 1917): the Italian cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape

ledger.note: 24 October 1917: the Austrians break through at Caporetto. 'On 24 October 1917, Austrians ... attacked at Caporetto'; Italy had attacked Austria-Hungary in May 1915. The page does not say how far the advance went; the region is the Italian cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape beyond the 1912 outline.

region.text: the Ukrainian and Moldovan cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape beyond the 1912 outline: the zone the Central Powers held after Brest-Litovsk and the Ukrainian treaty

ledger.note: 18 February 1918: Operation Faustschlag (infobox '18 February - 3 March 1918'): 'the German and Austro-Hungarian forces started a major three-pronged offensive'; 'Ukrainian troops and the Austro-Hungarian Army had secured Odessa'; after Brest-Litovsk 'capturing the whole of Ukraine'. The page maps no Austro-Hungarian zone, so the Ukrainian and Moldovan cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape remain the region (unverified extent).

region.text: northern Albania, where the troops took 'Scutari and finally Durazzo at the end of February' 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape

ledger.note: September 1918: 'In September 1918, the Entente forces broke through the Central Powers' lines north of Thessaloniki, and within days Austro-Hungarian forces began to withdraw from Albania' (Principality of Albania page; the albania dossier /ledger/5 has the same). The page gives no day.

region.text: Montenegro, which Austria-Hungary 'defeated and occupied' in January 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape beyond the 1912 outline

ledger.note: October 1918: Austria-Hungary 'occupied Montenegro from 15 January 1916 to October 1918' (Kingdom of Montenegro page; the montenegro dossier /ledger/12 has the same). The Montenegrin campaign page is silent on the end. The Podgorica Assembly followed on 26 November 1918 (the page's lead says 28 November).

region.text: Czechia and Slovakia: 'Czech politicians peacefully took over command in Prague on 28 October'; 'On the same day, the Czechs and Slovaks formally proclaimed the establishment of Czechoslovakia as an independent state'; 'On 30 October, the Slovaks did the same'

ledger.note: 28-30 October 1918: Czech politicians take over in Prague (28 October), the Czechs and Slovaks proclaim Czechoslovakia (28 October) and the Slovaks do the same on 30 October; Czechoslovakia is the infobox successor. The page gives the lands only as 'Czechs and Slovaks'; the region is Czechia plus Slovakia, as the czechoslovakia dossier founds the state (/ledger/0). Carpathian Ruthenia is under hungarian-republic until April 1919.

region.text: the South Slav lands: 'On 29 October, the Slavs in both portions of what remained of Austria-Hungary proclaimed the' State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs; Istria goes to Italy (next entry); the three cells of the outline that lie in modern Montenegro are the Dalmatian coast (reading)

ledger.note: 29 October 1918: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is proclaimed; the page's sentence names 'the Slavs in both portions of what remained of Austria-Hungary'. Lands: Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, as Saint-Germain gives 'Most of Dalmatia, Carniola, and Lower Styria' and Bosnia and Herzegovina to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes; Istria is taken out for Italy and Vojvodina goes to the Serbian entry.

region.text: Hungary and Carpathian Ruthenia: Karolyi 'formally repudiate[d] the compromise agreement on 31 October' and proclaimed the Hungarian Democratic Republic on 16 November; Carpathian Ruthenia stayed Hungarian until April 1919 (czechoslovakia dossier /ledger/2)

ledger.note: 31 October 1918: Hungary repudiates the Compromise of 1867 ('On 17 October 1918, the Hungarian Parliament voted in favour of terminating the union with Austria'); 'Karolyi followed suit on 16 November, proclaiming the Hungarian Democratic Republic'. Region: Hungary plus Carpathian Ruthenia, which the czechoslovakia dossier gains from hungarian-republic in April 1919 (the Trianon page: 'Carpathian Ruthenia, which became part of Czechoslovakia').

region.text: Austria: the German-Austrian National Council 'proclaimed the Republic of German Austria'; the State Council was created on 30 October 1918 as the executive body

ledger.note: 30 October 1918: German-Austria acts as a state. The German-Austria page: on 21 October 1918 the deputies declared they would 'form an independent German-Austrian state'; on 30 October 'the State Council was created as an executive body'; on 12 November the National Assembly 'officially declared German-Austria a republic' (infobox 'Austrian Republic: 12 November 1918'; Austria-Hungary page); name changed to Republic of Austria on 21 October 1919. The page does not call 30 October a proclamation; it is dated to the dissolution month because a split cannot follow the end of the state.

region.text: western Galicia and the Polish part of Cieszyn Silesia: the Polish Liquidation Committee, 'Created on 28 October 1918' at Krakow, to keep order in 'the former Austrian part of partitioned Poland'; Saint-Germain: 'The former Galicia fell back to the re-established Polish Republic'

ledger.note: 28 October 1918: the Polish Liquidation Committee is 'Created on 28 October 1918' by Polish members of the Austrian parliament, seat Krakow, to keep order in 'the former Austrian part of partitioned Poland'; infobox successors of Austria-Hungary: 'Polish Liquidation Committee', 'Kingdom of Poland'. The page names no lands, so the region is the outline's cells in modern Poland (western Galicia, the Polish part of Cieszyn Silesia); Saint-Germain: 'The former Galicia fell back to the re-established Polish Republic'. Eastern Galicia is in the West Ukrainian entry. The Committee handed over to Warsaw on 27 March 1919.

region.text: eastern Galicia: 'The West Ukrainian People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 November 1918' and 'controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919'; the outline's Ukrainian cells minus Carpathian Ruthenia (hungarian-republic) and Bukovina (Romania)

ledger.note: 1 November 1918: 'The West Ukrainian People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 November 1918' at Lviv, 'Until November 13, 1918, the state was officially known as the Ukrainian State'; it 'controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919'. Dated to the dissolution month (31 October) so that the split does not follow the end of the monarchy. The state also 'claimed the northern part of Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia'; those claims are not drawn. Infobox successor; needs a dossier.

region.text: Transylvania, the Romanian Banat, Crisana, Maramures and all of Bukovina: '28 November. The union of Bukovina with Romania is declared'; 'the union of Transylvania with the Kingdom of Romania on 1 December 1918'; Trianon: 'Romania received the territories of Transylvania, part of Banat and other territories from Hungary'

ledger.note: 28 November 1918 (Bukovina) and 1 December 1918 (Transylvania): 'The union of Bukovina with Romania is declared' and 'the union of Transylvania with the Kingdom of Romania on 1 December 1918'; Trianon confirmed 'Transylvania, part of Banat and other territories'. Dated to the dissolution because the land left the monarchy with it; the Romanian dossier books the gains in /ledger/27-28 (November and December 1918). The page does not name Crisana or Maramures; the region is the outline's cells in modern Romania plus all of Bukovina (the northern part claimed by the West Ukrainian state is kept with Romania, as the Romanian dossier gains Bukovina whole).

region.text: Vojvodina (Banat, Backa, Baranja, Syrmia) and the Serbian bank of the Sava: the Great National Assembly at Novi Sad 'on 25 November 1918' proclaimed the secession of 'Banat, Bačka and Baranja' from the 'already collapsed Austria-Hungary' and their unification with the Kingdom of Serbia

ledger.note: 25 November 1918: the Great National Assembly at Novi Sad 'declared the accession' of 'Banat, Bačka and Baranja' to the Kingdom of Serbia, seceding from the 'already collapsed Austria-Hungary'; Syrmia joined on 24 November (serbs dossier /ledger/28). Dated to the dissolution month because the monarchy's authority ended on 31 October; the serbs dossier books the gains in November 1918. The region adds the Serbian bank of the Sava (Zemun, three cells) to the gazetteer's Vojvodina.

region.text: Trentino, South Tyrol and the Austrian Littoral: 'The southern half of the former Tyrolean crownland up to the Brenner Pass' and 'the Austrian Littoral' with Trieste and Istria went to Italy (Saint-Germain, 10 September 1919)

ledger.note: 3 November 1918 (occupation) and 10 September 1919 (treaty): Saint-Germain gave Italy 'The southern half of the former Tyrolean crownland up to the Brenner Pass' and 'the Austrian Littoral', 'the Imperial Free City of Trieste' and Istria; the Villa Giusti armistice was signed on 3 November 1918 (Austria-Hungary page). Dated to the dissolution month; the kingdom-of-italy dossier books Trentino-Alto Adige and Trieste in 1919 (/ledger/15). The Slovenian part of the Littoral cannot be named with the gazetteer and stays in the Slovenes-Croats-Serbs entry.

region.text: the monarchy

ledger.note: 31 October 1918: Austria-Hungary dissolves. Infobox 'Empire dissolved: 31 October 1918'; the Imperial Manifesto of 16 October, 'the armistice was signed at Villa Giusti on 3 November', 'On 11 November, Karl issued a carefully worded proclamation'; Treaty of Saint-Germain 10 September 1919, Treaty of Trianon 4 June 1920.

region.text: Serbia, which 'was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria': the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape in Serbia, Kosovo and North Macedonia beyond the 1912 outline (Vojvodina was already Hungarian)

ledger.note: 1 November 1918: Serbian forces enter Belgrade after the Vardar Offensive of September 1918. 'Serbian forces entered Belgrade on 1 November 1918.'

region.text: Friuli and the Veneto plain beyond the 1912 outline, taken after Caporetto (24 October 1917): the Italian cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape

ledger.note: 3 November 1918: the armistice of Villa Giusti. 'the armistice was signed at Villa Giusti on 3 November'; the page does not describe the withdrawal from the occupied Italian ground.

region.text: the Romanian cells of Cliopatria's 1917 shape beyond the 1912 outline: Wallachia and the Dobruja zone after the fall of Bucharest on 6 December 1916

ledger.note: November 1918 (page silent): the occupation of Wallachia ends with the Central Powers' collapse. The page records 'On 7 May 1918 Romania signed the Treaty of Bucharest with the Central Powers'; the end of the occupation is not on it. Romanian Campaign page: Mackensen 'was appointed as the military governor of the occupied territories of Romania' and the Treaty of Bucharest (7 May 1918) ceded Carpathian passes to Austria-Hungary (Eastern Front page); no region is named, so no gain is recorded.

region.text: the Ukrainian and Moldovan cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape beyond the 1912 outline: the zone the Central Powers held after Brest-Litovsk and the Ukrainian treaty

ledger.note: November 1918 (page silent): the Austro-Hungarian zone in Ukraine ends with the collapse; no date on the page. Operation Faustschlag page: silent on the end of the Austro-Hungarian occupation.

region.text: the Austro-Hungarian Military General Government of Lublin, which 'covered the southern parts of Russian Poland'

ledger.note: November 1918: infobox 'Armistice, withdrawal of German forces: 3 November 1918'; Governor Anton Liposcak 'resigned on 2 November 1918' after Austria-Hungary dissolved. The page names no Polish successor body here; the Polish Liquidation Committee (28 October 1918, Krakow) is the second-polish-republic entry.

wars.name: Occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (1878)

zones.text: the provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina

wars.outcome: 'The occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina started on 29 July 1878 and was over on 20 October'; Bosnia stayed Ottoman in law until the annexation of October 1908.
wars.note: A name for the event as the Condominium page describes it, not a Wikipedia war title. The Congress of Berlin was held 'in June and July 1878'.

wars.name: Serbian campaign of World War I

zones.text: Serbia, which 'was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria': the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape in Serbia, Kosovo and North Macedonia beyond the 1912 outline (Vojvodina was already Hungarian)

wars.outcome: The Central Powers' offensive of 6 October 1915 ended on 24 November 1915; Serbia 'was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria'; Serbian forces entered Belgrade on 1 November 1918.
wars.note: 'Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914'; the Battle of Cer was 'the first Allied victory in World War I' (undated on the page). Bulgaria and Germany are named by the page as the other Central Powers in the 1915 offensive only by implication ('under German command', 'divided between ... Bulgaria').

wars.name: Montenegrin campaign

zones.text: Montenegro, which Austria-Hungary 'defeated and occupied' in January 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape beyond the 1912 outline
northern Albania, where the troops took 'Scutari and finally Durazzo at the end of February' 1916: the cells of Cliopatria's 1916 shape

wars.outcome: Austro-Hungarian victory in the infobox dates 5-17 January 1916; Cetinje fell on 13 January, a provisional military government was set up on 1 March, and Scutari and Durazzo were taken at the end of February.
wars.note: The page does not give the extent of the occupation zone in Albania.

wars.name: Eastern Front (World War I)

zones.text: Galicia, 'the Russians controlling almost all of that region by the end of 1914'
Transylvania and southern Bukovina: the 102 Romanian cells that Cliopatria's 1916 shape loses against 1912 (Romanian troops marched into Transylvania on 27 August 1916)
the Romanian cells of Cliopatria's 1917 shape beyond the 1912 outline: Wallachia and the Dobruja zone after the fall of Bucharest on 6 December 1916
the Ukrainian and Moldovan cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape beyond the 1912 outline: the zone the Central Powers held after Brest-Litovsk and the Ukrainian treaty

wars.outcome: Russia held almost all of Galicia by the end of 1914 and lost it again from May 1915; Romania entered on 27 August 1916 and lost Bucharest on 6 December; the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (3 March 1918) and the Treaty of Bucharest (7 May 1918) closed the front.
wars.note: The page gives no date for the fall of Lemberg, Przemysl or Czernowitz, for the Ukrainian treaty (9 February 1918) or the occupation of Ukraine.

wars.name: Italian Front (World War I)

zones.text: Friuli and the Veneto plain beyond the 1912 outline, taken after Caporetto (24 October 1917): the Italian cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape

wars.outcome: 'In May 1915, Italy attacked Austria-Hungary'; 'On 24 October 1917, Austrians ... attacked at Caporetto'; the armistice was signed at Villa Giusti on 3 November 1918.
wars.note: The war's own article was not opened (page budget); the zone is the Italian cells of Cliopatria's 1918 shape.

certainty.note: The monarchy's frontiers are treaty lines of the period (the page cites the Congress of Berlin); the Sanjak garrison and the Bosnian occupation (1878-1908) are drawn on the Congress's lines.
The war-years fronts and occupation zones (Galicia, Serbia, Montenegro, Albania, Romania, Italy, Ukraine) are moving or unmapped by the pages; the monarchy's own pre-war frontier stays sharp.

notes: BUDGET. Five pages (Austria-Hungary, Condominium of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Eastern Front, Serbian campaign, Montenegrin campaign) for 12 Cliopatria shapes; the Italian Front, Ukrainian occupation and Albanian occupation are therefore only partly dated. DIFFERENT STATES: Cliopatria's Wikidata id Q28513 is shared by this row, by hungarian-nationalists (the Hungarian revolutionary state of 1848-49, and Hungary in 1956-57) and by hungary (1947-2024); they are different states, none a duplicate of this one, so no merge. WHAT WAS CORRECTED. (1) 1880-1907: Cliopatria draws occupied Bosnia and the Sanjak as Austro-Hungarian land from 1880 (two years after the 29 July 1878 occupation) although the pages say Bosnia was occupied but not annexed until 5 October 1908 and the Sanjak was occupied 1878-1909; both are ledger occupations, the 1873 outline is the base. (2) 1908: a new keyframe adds annexed Bosnia without the Sanjak, which Cliopatria keeps to 1910. (3) 1915-1918: Cliopatria draws every foreign-held zone as Austro-Hungarian land and Russian-held Galicia as loss; the corrections use the 1912 outline and carry both as occupation events (counterpart = the occupied or occupying state). (4) The Tianjin concession: Cliopatria adds two cells in 1905 and drops them in 1917; neither page mentions it (confidence 1). NOT SETTLED: the extent of the Austro-Hungarian zones in Romania, Ukraine/Moldova and Italy (the shape cells are used as the region); Bukovina's Russian occupation dates; the Treaty of Bucharest's border changes; whether the 1917 shape's 7 Bulgarian cells are an artefact. The Austrian Empire dossier of this project applies the 1853 Austrian outline to Hungary 1849-1852; Cliopatria's Austrian Empire shape of 1866-1867 omits 220 Czech cells that this shape includes from 1868. Counterpart slugs without a file: state-of-slovenes-croats-and-serbs (new), ukrainian-people-s-republic (row starts 1919), czechoslovakia and republic-of-austria and hungarian-republic (rows start 1919), united-principalities-of-moldavia-and-wallachia stands for Romania in 1916-1918 (Kingdom of Romania row starts 1919). SECOND PASS (2026-11-01, after review): (1) 1918 hand-off completed: the 1912 outline (2,645 cells) is split between czechoslovakia (Czechia and Slovakia, 515 cells), republic-of-austria (331), hungarian-republic (Hungary and Carpathian Ruthenia, 418), the State of Slovenes Croats and Serbs (455), kingdom-of-italy (Italy and Istria, 71), second-polish-republic (152), west-ukrainian-people-s-republic (eastern Galicia, 182), the Romanian dossier (Romania and all Bukovina, 431) and serbs (Vojvodina and the Serbian bank of the Sava, 76); no overlap; 14 cells stay unassigned (11 on the German side of the Bavarian and Bohemian frontier, 2 Chinese cells at Tianjin lost in 1917, 1 coast cell), border noise of Cliopatria's shape. The splits are dated 1918/10, the dissolution month; where a successor acted later (West Ukrainian republic 1 November, Serbia 24-25 November, Romania 28 November and 1 December, Italy 1919) the date is in the note and the successor's own dossier carries the gain. The pages give no lands for Romania, Galicia or Vojvodina in the Austria-Hungary article; each successor's land rests on its own page and, for Crisana, Maramures, Istria's extent and the three Montenegrin cells (Dalmatian coast), on the researcher's reading. (2) Russian-held Galicia and Bukovina: empire boundary March 1917, Provisional Government March-August 1917 (counterpart russian-republic, whose dossier starts 14 September 1917), end 3 August 1917 (Czernowitz). (3) Tianjin concession dated from its page: 27 December 1902 to 14 August 1917. (4) Romanian incursion ended 25 October 1916. (5) Montenegro (October 1918) and Albania (September 1918) occupation ends taken from their own country pages. (6) Operation Faustschlag dates the Ukraine occupation from 18 February 1918. (7) New: the Military General Government of Lublin 1915-1918. STILL OPEN: extents of the Ukrainian, Moldovan, Wallachian and Italian zones; the Italian-held strip on the Isonzo (Gorizia, 1916-1917) is not recorded; the Slovenian part of the Austrian Littoral is inside the Slovenes-Croats-Serbs entry although Saint-Germain gives the Littoral to Italy.
